source.title: Dimensional Criticality at Grokking Across MLPs and Transformers

page_placements.theme: Non-circuit diagnostics of grokking and overfitting

record.tranche_reason: The study reports a behavioral grokking trajectory on modular addition and uses a new gradient-cascade measurement to analyze its timing and early-warning properties; it is not an explicit replication of the original method.
record.gate_note: The paper describes a representative ModAdd-59 train–test delay and analyzes gradient-cascade dimensions around grokking. The XOR task has no train/test split, as the paper explicitly notes, so it is not evidence for delayed test generalization. The dimension-crossing results are relevant to grokking but do not directly test any listed version; they are recorded under fits_no_version. The paper's circuit-level gradual-formation and optimizer/numerical-artifact claims are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study reproduces canonical ModAdd grokking (80/20 split, Adam with weight decay) as the setting for a new gradient-cascade diagnostic, TDU–OFC D(t). Its reported results concern that diagnostic: the D=1 crossing, phase-split exponents, early-warning divergence and shadow-probe controls. Fig. 1 shows one representative delayed-generalization run, but only qualitatively, and training-set size is never varied. The early-warning result tracks gradient-cascade geometry, not a generalizing circuit or the removal of memorizing components. So no listed version is tested by the study's own results. XOR has no train/test split and cannot show delayed generalization.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim grokking in ModAdd Transformers and XOR MLPs coincides with an opposite-direction crossing of D=1, which they read as a shared critical attractor. They propose a 'Dimensional Grokking Principle' and present D(t) as a macroscopic order parameter and early-warning signal. They acknowledge the coverage is only two tasks and two architectures.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a TDU–OFC offline gradient-cascade probe and grokking-aligned finite-size scaling rather than reproducing the original grokking method. It analyzes Transformers on modular addition and MLPs on XOR.
record.method_sensitivity: For XOR, a sweep over α∈{0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5} and threshold percentiles {85th, 90th, 95th} reports grokking-timing variation below 3% (p>0.7, not significant); threshold percentile is described as having negligible effect. Shadow-probe differences in D are bounded by 0.14 for ModAdd and 0.11 for XOR in the critical window.

fits_no_version.finding: Grokked and ungrokked ModAdd-59 trajectories diverge in gradient-cascade dimension 100–200 epochs before behavioral grokking (D≈1.02 vs 1.75 at epoch 100). Ungrokked runs stay at D>1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A gradient-geometry (cascade-dimension) measure separates runs that will grok from those that won't, before the behavioral transition.

fits_no_version.finding: Near grokking, D(t) crosses D=1: it descends for ModAdd (p=59, p=47) and ascends for XOR, with pre/post phase exponents of 1.12 and 0.92.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A gradient-cascade scaling dimension crosses the Gaussian baseline D=1 at grokking, with task-dependent direction.

record.code_released: not stated; analysis scripts and data are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request
record.problems: The evidence covers two tasks and two architectures. The representative behavioral trajectory is reported qualitatively, and the study does not vary training-set size. XOR has no train/test split, so it cannot establish delayed test generalization. Data and scripts are available only upon reasonable request.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out. Shadow-probe and synthetic-gradient controls concern the validity of the new diagnostic rather than the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Only one qualitative representative trajectory is shown. There are no accuracy numbers at chance or near-perfect levels, and no variation of training-set size or its effect on the delay.
No circuit identification, Fourier analysis, or tracking of memorizing-component removal. The early-warning measure is gradient geometry, not circuit formation.
Not tested: no non-algorithmic data and no manipulation of initialization scale or weight norm.
Not tested: weight decay is fixed at 1e-3, with no critical dataset size and no ungrokking. Weight-decay suppression is mentioned only as a prediction.
Not tested: the optimizer (Adam) is fixed and numerical precision is not varied.

missing.what: Grokking epochs span g∈[29,3000] across d_model 16–128. The delay varies strongly with model width; this is not a listed version, but it is context for V1.

record.verdict_notes: I classified this study as T4: grokking is reproduced as a precondition and the results concern the new probe. The reader's V2 'supports' label conflates a gradient-geometry early warning with V2's circuit-level mechanism, so I removed it. The XOR 'grokking' is an abrupt learning event on four shared patterns, not delayed test generalization. The code is not released.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not compare training-set sizes or report how delay changes as the training set shrinks. The representative trajectory is described qualitatively; it does not state that training accuracy is perfect or test accuracy is at chance.

The paper reports an early-warning gradient-geometry measure, but does not identify a generalizing circuit, test Fourier algorithms, track removal of memorizing components, or establish that circuit formation is gradual.

rows.subject: ModAdd-59 Transformer, representative run
rows.operation_detail: Train on the modular-addition task and measure train/test accuracy over epochs.
rows.measure: Training and test accuracy over training
rows.note: The text describes early training-accuracy saturation followed by delayed test generalization; the plotted values are not reported numerically in the text. The figure marks g=228. The paper does not test the effect of training-set size.
rows.check: Figure-only setup confirmation of the grokking setting (g=228). No train or test accuracy values are given, so chance-to-near-perfect cannot be read, and the training-set-size dependence is not examined. It serves as precondition evidence, not a test.

rows.subject: ModAdd-59 Transformer grokked runs

rows.value: D ≈ 1.02 at epoch 100; trajectories diverge 100–200 epochs before behavioral grokking
rows.note: The paper reports this as an early-warning separation between grokked and ungrokked trajectories; ΔD ≈ 0.73.
rows.check: D is a gradient-cascade scaling exponent produced by the study's own probe. It is not a circuit-level progress measure as V2 names, so the link to V2 is wrong. The early-warning divergence belongs under fits_no_version.

relation.reason: The study directly measures the canonical delayed-generalization behavior in ModAdd-59, in addition to analyzing gradient-cascade geometry. Fig. 1 supplies evidence on V1; the cascade diagnostic alone does not test V2's circuit-formation account.

tranche.reason: The study introduces a different diagnostic but also reports its own behavioral evidence bearing on V1: Section III(A) and Fig. 1 show early training saturation followed by delayed test generalization, with grokking at epoch 228. Its results are not confined to diagnostic performance. Dependence of delay on training-set size is untested.

source_check.notes: D is an exponent fitted across model sizes, not an individual-run or circuit-formation measure; grokked and ungrokked populations contain 35 and 12 runs, respectively. XOR uses the same four examples for training and evaluation and is explicitly distinguished from canonical delayed generalization.
